minutes.headline: Assessors weighed an ad hoc neighborhood review committee, website redesign, exemptions research, and ended in executive session on abatements.
minutes.summary: The Board of Assessors heard a staff status report (abatements filed, inspections done), signed revised/omitted and motor vehicle commitments, and discussed a MUNIS tax-bill error. Most of the meeting went to a proposed neighborhood review team, the assessing calendar, exemptions and deferrals research, and a long reorganization of the assessors' web pages. The board then moved into executive session on abatement applications; a count is not captured.

public_comment.topic: Chair asked for public comment; no one in the room or on Zoom spoke.
Second call for public comment at end of meeting; no one present.

votes.motion: Enter executive session under purpose 7 (c.59 s.60, abatement/exemption applications confidential), not to return to open session.

budget_items.what_was_said: A solar project under a 20-year agreement with the town underpaid, so a revised assessment was committed.
A commitment of motor vehicle abatements was signed by the board.
The second excise commitment of 2024 was signed.
A further abatement commitment spanning several years was signed.
A consultant review would need a contract, and the town manager should be consulted on cost first.
Approval for a data collector was received but hiring cannot occur until after the new year; admin position still unfilled.
Deferral has no state reimbursement, a maximum three-year term and a recommended interest rate.

decisions.decision: Neighborhood review team to be led by a board member; composition of about five members (lake resident, non-lake resident, realtor, outside assessor, board member), to be identified by the next meeting.
Chair to announce the committee volunteer search at public comment at the next day's Select Board meeting and on the website.
The town manager's baseline assessing calendar will be used as the base; the chair will add other items next week.
Exemptions and deferrals research to produce a clear status by early October, with any action in November; one member took 41A, another 41C/D.

Website top-level order reworked: agendas, minutes and forms first, then recent news, tax rate information, find your house, facts, then resources; a revised outline will be circulated before the next meeting.
Documents for the board must be put on a posted agenda rather than emailed; a proposed open meeting law communication flowchart will return to the board after the town counsel reviews it.
A policy on responding to signature requests within 10 business days to be written up, possibly with town counsel.
Tentative meetings: May 20, June 3, June 10, then monthly in July and August, dates tentative.
Staff to run a report of parcels with site index zero.

what_happened.line: The Board of Assessors agreed that a neighborhood review team would be led by a board member, with about five members to be identified by the next meeting.
The board signed a revised assessment for a solar project that underpaid under its 20-year agreement, and signed motor vehicle abatement and excise commitments.
A MUNIS tax bill error on exemptions was discussed; corrected bills are to be sent before July 1.
The board agreed to use the town manager's draft assessing calendar as its base and to reorder the assessors' web pages, with a revised outline to be circulated.
The board moved into executive session on abatement applications; the vote count was not captured.

why_it_matters: The solar revision, the corrected exemption bills and the abatement commitments each change what particular taxpayers owe, and the review team is a step toward how neighborhoods are valued in future assessments.
Research on exemptions and deferrals is due to produce a clear status by early October, so any new relief for residents would come after that, with action in November.
watch_next: Identification of the neighborhood review team members, due by the next meeting, tentatively May 20.
The exemptions and deferrals status, due by early October, with any action in November.
